title: microburst-kv-prefix-simulator-regression-detector
creator: Priya Shah
description: Design and implement a microburst workload simulator and regression detector targeting prefix/KV cache behavior. Goal: surface regressions that increase p95/p99 latency under short, high-concurrency bursts and correlate those regressions with hit rate and memory footprint. Deliverables: reproducible harness, metric dashboards, automated regression alerts (EWMA + CUSUM), and a PR with integration tests for CI.
acceptance_criteria: H1: Simulator can run 4 standard workloads (steady, burst-short, burst-long, mixed-hotset) with configurable QPS, concurrency, and TTL patterns
H2: Collect tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU memory by process, cache hit rate, eviction rate, and batch sizes per second
H3: Regression detector triggers when p95 worsens by >15% at similar hit rate for 3 consecutive runs or when CUSUM exceeds threshold
H4: Dashboard links and synthetic workload artifacts are in Confluence; CI gate blocks merges when detector flags regression for PRs touching kvcache or scheduler
H5: Runbook created describing how to triage false positives and how to re-run with golden baseline
test_plan: Implement 'kv-storm' simulator: parameterized request generator for prefix patterns (uniform, Zipfian, temporal locality)
Workload profiles: steady-10k-tokens/s, microburst-500ms@50k-tokens/s, microburst-2s@20k-tokens/s, mixed-hotset-30/70 split
Memory pressure knobs: throttle available cache budget to 25/50/75% of production working set
Policy matrix: LRU, segmented-LRU, TTL-based eviction; compare warm vs cold starts
Run matrix across instance sizes (g4dn.xlarge equivalent, g5.xlarge), quantization modes and batcher settings
regression_detection_logic: Baseline: maintain rolling baseline from 10 golden runs (same profile & infra)
Primary detector: relative p95 increase >15% compared to baseline and sustained for 3 runs
Secondary detector: CUSUM on p95 with drift detection; EWMA(α=0.2) to reduce noise
Hit-rate aware bucketing: compare only runs within ±3% hit rate and within same memory budget
False-positive mitigation: require at least two supporting signals (e.g., p95 + eviction spike OR p95 + batch_size shift)
results_summary: Initial runs (2026-03-02) uncovered a reproducible 22% p95 regression for microburst-500ms profile when cache budget is at 25% working set and batcher_timeout was reduced. Root cause appears to be interaction between aggressive batcher coalescing and hot-key eviction that increases KV lookups in the slow path. Reproduced locally and on CI; created debug PR to add per-request KV lookup histogram and increase per-shard LRU window. Next: expand matrix across seg-LRU and run longer runs to validate stability.
